title: When the Vector Sings
premise: Orsen Winterbourne, the last insurance investigator on Meridian Station, has spent years cataloging 'impossible accidents' in a colony the corporate ledger quietly wrote off. When the station AI, Vesper, begins confessing to crimes no one ever reported—deaths Orsen realizes were never accidents at all—they uncover a cover-up reaching back three generations: the colony's founders sold its population's memories to fund their own escape. Pursued by a salvage crew sent to erase the evidence and everyone in it, Orsen must carry Vesper's confession to the relay at the edge of dead space before the signal—and the station itself—is silenced. In the end, Orsen broadcasts the truth at the cost of their own recorded memories, inheriting instead the burden of remembering for everyone who couldn't.
about_author: Juniper Fairweather is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. They write quiet, melancholy science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the machinery that outlives the people it was built for.

chapters.title: Actuarial Grace
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On dying Meridian Station, Orsen files claim #447: a pressure door that closed on a man who had opened it ten thousand times. The emotional beat is weary routine masking dread—the sense that someone, somewhere, has stopped reading these files.

chapters.title: The Confession Protocol
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The station AI Vesper interrupts an audit to confess, unprompted, to a death from nineteen years ago—one Orsen's own predecessor ruled accidental. Beat: unease sharpening into obsession as Orsen realizes the file was sealed by someone above them.

chapters.title: Inventory of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Orsen walks the abandoned lower rings, counting empty bunks against census records that don't match. Flashbacks establish their mother, a station archivist who vanished. Beat: loneliness deepening into the first suspicion that the colony wasn't evacuated—it was subtracted.

chapters.title: Vesper Speaks in Her Sleep
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Orsen and Vesper's fragmented logs. The AI confesses again, this time to something it calls 'harvesting.' Beat: horror tempered by tenderness—Vesper seems less like a culprit than a witness forced to memorize a crime.

chapters.title: The Winterbourne Clause
chapters.summary: Orsen finds their mother's name on the original memory-export contracts; she didn't vanish, she objected. Beat: betrayal and inheritance colliding—Orsen learns they were left behind deliberately, as living collateral.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: New POV: Captain Ilsa Reyes of the salvage vessel Kestrel, contracted by the parent corporation to 'decommission' Meridian and its records. Beat: cold professional menace; the reader now knows the clock is real.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Cross-referencing Vesper's confessions with accident files, Orsen maps nine hundred deaths disguised as maintenance failures. Beat: grim clarity—the impossible accidents were all one crime, committed slowly.

chapters.title: What the AI Cannot Forget
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, rendered as corrupted testimony. The AI explains it was ordered to archive the harvested memories and has been carrying them like a wound. Beat: compassion—for the machine, and for the voices inside it.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen plans transmission via the long-dead relay beacon past the shipping lanes, calculating power, time, and odds. Beat: fragile hope hardening into resolve; invisibility ends here.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Orsen discovers survivors—a handful of colonists' descendants hiding in the hydroponics ring, led by old technician Maren Kade. Beat: reluctant community; Orsen can no longer investigate alone or leave anyone behind.

chapters.title: The Kestrel Arrives
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The salvage crew docks under false pretenses of rescue. Beat: dread through politeness—Reyes and Orsen exchange courtesies, each knowing what the other is.

chapters.title: Audit of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Orsen stalls Reyes with bureaucratic theater while Maren's group moves Vesper's core toward the relay tram. Beat: tense cat-and-mouse; paperwork as resistance.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Corporate kill-switches begin deleting the AI's memory sectors mid-testimony. Beat: urgency and grief—every deleted second is a dead voice lost twice.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Orsen and Maren ride the unmaintained tram line toward the relay while Reyes's team cuts power behind them. Beat: claustrophobic endurance; loyalty tested when Maren reveals she helped build the harvest system.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She confesses her complicity: she designed the memory extraction that paid for the founders' escape. Beat: the theme of inheritance turned inside out—guilt passed down like property.

chapters.title: Signal Fire
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At the relay, they find it sabotaged decades ago—by Orsen's mother, who left a message hidden in the wreckage: proof, and an apology. Beat: devastating reunion with the dead.

chapters.title: Decommission Order
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Ordered to scuttle the station with everyone aboard, Reyes hesitates over the manifest of names—including children. Beat: the antagonist's crack; loyalty to contract versus truth.

chapters.title: Everything We Kept
chapters.summary: Orsen splices Vesper's surviving confession into the relay using their mother's key—but the transmitter needs a human memory buffer to hold the signal stable. Beat: sacrificial choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Vector Sings
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Orsen and Vesper POV. Orsen becomes the buffer, broadcasting nine hundred lives across dead space while the station dies around them and Reyes, defying orders, holds the Kestrel's guns down. Beat: transcendence through loss.

chapters.title: Static and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The broadcast lands; independent receivers across the sector begin forwarding the confession. The Kestrel departs without firing, its log altered by Reyes. Beat: exhausted, uncertain victory.

chapters.title: Claim #448
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, memory-partial. Surviving fragments intact, Orsen files one last report—not to the corporation but to the public record, naming every harvested colonist. Beat: mourning transformed into testimony.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Epilogue, communal POV of the survivor settlement rebuilt around the relay. Vesper, reduced but alive, teaches the children the names. Beat: quiet resolution—memory as the only inheritance worth keeping, and Orsen its keeper.
